—¿Te acuestas con una mujer distinta cada noche? —preguntó Caitlyn, con la misma naturalidad con que alguien comenta el pronóstico del tiempo.
—Mmm… ¿hola? ¿Cómo estás? —respondió Vi, con un goteo de ironía—. Eso es lo que pregunta la gente normal antes de ponerse a charlar, princesa.
—¿Por qué lo haces? —insistió Caitlyn—. ¿No crees en las relaciones?
—Eso es un cuento de hadas para gente que tiene tiempo de sobra. Aquí no hay sitio para eso.
—No creo que sea así. No debería serlo.
—Entonces supongo que sigues esperando a tu príncipe azul.
—A una princesa, en realidad.
Piltover levanta sus nuevas fuerzas militares para frenar el creciente terrorismo de Zaun, que ha convertido la muerte de Silco en el martirio perfecto para su causa. Pero los recursos son finitos, y gran parte de esos soldados son convictos de Stillwater a los que se les ofrece su única y gran oportunidad de redención: convertirse en los reclutas de Punta Coria. Cuando la lealtad se compra con libertad y el deseo no entiende de uniformes. ¿Dónde estará la lealtad de cada uno?

summary:
“Ja-yce...”
It was speaking. Calling. Almost pleading, in a way. Jayce felt a chill rolling down his spine like icy fingertips. He could only bring himself to stare, eyes wide and full of a mix of emotions he couldn’t begin to identify at the moment. In fact, Jayce was finding it hard to identify anything at all at this moment. Only the midnight shadows and that deep, raspy, punctuated accent that was far too familiar and yet so ungodly foreign.
“Jayce.” It called again, this time more clearly.
Jayce felt his chest grow tighter as he scanned the hunched figure. Deformed and mangled beyond any recognition of something close to human. The curve and bend of its spine was unnatural to that of this world. Limbs long and extending towards the floor as it stood limp. Its body was made of muscle. But, the worst part was the eyes. They were so…uncanny. Pitch black, glossed over with a single shred of life. Jayce felt like he was staring at the face of death; yet so incredibly familiar…
Jayce swallowed the dryness of his mouth, a deep, cold fear setting into his bones as he continued to stare at the horrors that have broken into his lab tonight.
“...Viktor?”

The dead did not answer prayers.
Jayce had learned that lesson long before the gods had ever heard him.
Not once did Viktor, the mage, the scholar, the truest architect of the arcane that Jayce could comprehend, find a way to converse with him. Though, that would be difficult in his current state; ashes and dust,and a stray piece of cane that survived the explosion, buried six feet below Faerun’s grounds in a pauper’s grave.
He prayed.
And prayed.
And he prayed until his voice would fail him.
“I know not who listens,” He would mutter beneath coarse, baited breath, “I do not know whose domain I trespass. But if there remains any power, any power that values truth over pride…mercy over ambition….then hear me.”
His hazel eyes would look up to plead if he knew it would find him absolution, but he had come to find the action futile.

“I didn’t want you to see,” Viktor says, as if it were the simplest thing.
“See what? What could we possibly have to hide from each other anymore?” But Viktor does not answer - nor does he appear to have any intention of doing so. Jayce presses, “Were you afraid it was going to make me angry? Or sad?”

Vi shifted beside her, head resting against her hands as she stared at the sky.
“There,” Vi’s voice broke the silence, her hand pointing upwards.
Caitlyn followed her direction. “Orion,” she whispered, turning slightly.
Vi smirked, her eyes never leaving the stars. “The Hunter… it reminds me of you.”
Caitlyn smiled, slowly inching closer to Vi, drawn to the steady heat that emanated from the knight.
“There’s another,” Vi breathed, pointing to a cluster of stars.
Caitlyn’s gaze darted across the sky. After a moment, she shook her head. “Where?”
“Here,” Vi murmured, offering her hand.
Caitlyn glanced to it for a moment, before lacing their hands together. The golden band on Vi’s ring finger caught the pale light of the moon as they moved.
After a moment she stilled, squeezing Caitlyn’s hand gently.
Caitlyn squinted, realisation soon dawning in her pupils. “Lupus...” she whispered, turning back to Vi.
Vi was already watching her, an intensity in her gaze that stole the air from Caitlyn’s lungs. Caitlyn edged closer, Vi’s breath ghosting over her lips.
“We’re struck amongst the stars,” Vi whispered, “the Hunter, and the Wolf.”

summary:
Viktor sniffed, hiding his wet eyes against Jayce’s shoulder, but he didn’t let go. His fingers stayed tangled in the fabric of Jayce’s gray sweatshirt.
“I’ve never had a friend like you,” he whispered, voice soft under the sounds of the forest. “Someone who is…”
“Kind of a loser?” Jayce offered.
“Gentle.” Viktor huffed a tiny, broken laugh. “But meeting your mom yesterday… I see where you got that gentleness from. W-Why you'd say things about loving people and finding them beautiful.”
The older boy shifted in the hug, no longer clinging, but letting himself enjoy it. He looked at Jayce, eyes still wet and shining, and Jayce couldn’t help brushing away the last tear that slipped down Viktor’s cheek.
From his eyes, Jayce’s gaze drifted to Viktor’s lips. He shouldn’t — this wasn’t the moment for that. But when he forced himself to look back up, he realized Viktor was staring at his lips too. A quiet, mutual confession.

title: as the ocean
author: taq
summary:
"You went outside," Caitlyn says. "How was it?"
How was it? How was the earth beneath her feet, the sky stretching out above her as far as she can see, the birds already out and about? The grass soft and wet, the flowers asleep but fragrant? The early morning sun still hidden behind the trees, a stray ray peeking out from between the leaves?

You match with a hot woman on a dating app.
You think she's the one.

She reveals to you that she's never slept with anyone before.

When Caitlyn and Vi match on the trendy new dating app in town, aka Bridge. Both of them end up getting way more than they bargained for. All signs point towards it not working out between their impossibly high incompatibility score and the small differences that make them polar opposites; believing their connection will withstand the test of time is fanciful at best. Fate, however, has a funny way of proving even the most logical systems wrong, and before either of them realise it, genuine feelings blossom between them. But when Vi makes an abrupt getaway in the middle of the night, it leads to a messy fallout, where both of them are left to pick up the shattered pieces, and an unforeseeable, but inevitable confession from Vi stops their romance dead in its tracks. Having survived the explosion at the Hex Tower and fled the smoldering wreckage of her life, Jinx hurtles toward the unforgiving, cold lands of Demacia. Wounded and haunted by the ghosts of her past, her path collides in a dark alley with that of Luxanna Crownguard, a noblewoman trapped by the weight of duty and forced to conceal a light that her own kingdom punishes with death.
As the anarchic chaos of Zaun and the forbidden magic of Demacia intertwine within the walls of a secret library, a dangerous facade is born: Lady Jishanna Aldergate. Tras sobrevivir a la explosión en la Torre Hex y huir de los restos humeantes de su vida, Jinx se precipita hacia las implacables y frías tierras de Demacia. Herida y atormentada por los fantasmas de su pasado, su camino se cruza en un oscuro callejón con el de Luxanna Crownguard, una noble atrapada por el peso del deber y obligada a ocultar una luz que su propio reino castiga con la muerte.
Mientras el caos anárquico de Zaun y la magia prohibida de Demacia se entrelazan entre los muros de una biblioteca secreta, nace una peligrosa fachada: Lady Jishanna Aldergate. Pero con los Cazadores de Magos al acecho y la sospecha del Comandante Garen, líder de la Vanguardia Valerosa, sobre ellos, su nuevo vínculo podría ser el santuario que las salve, o la chispa que lo encienda todo.

When Viktor blinks himself awake one morning with a distinct sense of wrongness he attributes it first to the immediate awareness that he is in Jayce's bedroom. In Jayce's bed. He knows exactly the contents of his desk and how the paintings are hung on his walls. And he knows for certain the rich scent of Jayce filling his lungs.

When he stumbles to the mirror, it feels like he might be looking through it. Into the living room. Into some other part of the apartment. Because his mind simply cannot process what he's seeing otherwise.
The face staring back at him isn't his own. It's Jayce's.
